primitives.label: Runneth
primitives.tagline: Runneth as a whole: the runtime behind every surface.
primitives.summary: The whole Runneth product. Use this when something affects everything at once rather than one specific area, like the model being slow, the runtime being down, or a change that touches every surface.
productFeatures: Does the work across web, Slack, apps, integrations, data, and routines.
Carries your workspace and org context into every conversation.
Runs on reviewed instructions, skills, and tools that the Motion team maintains.
userControls: Which workspace or org the work happens in.
Where you work with it: web, Slack, or an app.
The context, files, and instructions you give it.

thingsToKnow.summary: A provider outage hits everything.
thingsToKnow.detail: When the underlying model or runtime has an incident, every surface can slow down or fail at once. Start here when several things break together.

thingsToKnow.summary: It only sees the workspace it's in.
thingsToKnow.detail: Runneth can't see another workspace's work unless you ask it to and you have access.

primitives.label: Brain
primitives.tagline: What Runneth knows about your org.
primitives.summary: Where Runneth keeps what it knows: your standing rules, saved files and notes, templates, and the skills it can run. Use this for anything about saved context or how it remembers.
productFeatures: Reads your standing rules on every message, so they always apply.
Finds saved files and templates when they're relevant, instead of reading everything.
Keeps rules, files, templates, and skills as separate things.
userControls: The standing rules you save.
The files, notes, and references you save for reuse.
The templates and skills you set up for repeat work.

boxes.label: Standing rules
boxes.summary: Your always-on preferences and instructions. Read on every single message, so they always apply. Can be set for the whole org, a team, or one person.

boxes.label: Saved files
boxes.summary: Briefs, notes, transcripts, and references kept for reuse.

boxes.label: Templates
boxes.summary: Reusable formats for briefs, reports, and other deliverables.

boxes.label: Skills
boxes.summary: Step-by-step workflows Runneth can run when you ask.

thingsToKnow.summary: Standing rules always apply; saved files are matched.
thingsToKnow.detail: Rules are read every turn, but saved files are found by matching what you describe. A vaguely named file can get missed, so point Runneth at the right one if recall falls short.

thingsToKnow.summary: The brain only covers this org.
thingsToKnow.detail: It doesn't carry over to a different customer's setup.

primitives.label: Chat
primitives.tagline: The Motion chat window and live conversation.
primitives.summary: The chat window itself: sending messages, replies streaming in, starting a new conversation, and picking up where you left off. Use this when the conversation surface acts up but you can still work.
productFeatures: Starts and continues conversations in the web app.
Streams replies and shows progress as it works.
Links you out to the files, apps, and reports it creates.
userControls: Which workspace you're in.
Whether you continue a conversation or start a new one.
The message, file, or link you share when something looks off.

thingsToKnow.summary: A glitch in the window usually isn't lost data.
thingsToKnow.detail: A missing sidebar item or a first message that won't send is normally a display or startup hiccup. The conversation still exists underneath.

thingsToKnow.summary: Startup and waking from idle can stall.
thingsToKnow.detail: A reload normally brings it back.

primitives.label: Conversation history
primitives.tagline: How past chats are saved and found again.
primitives.summary: Your past web and Slack conversations: whether they show in the sidebar, whether old ones are findable, and continuity between web and Slack. Use this for recall and history questions.
productFeatures: Saves your web chats and Slack threads.
Pulls up past work by topic, person, date, or workspace when it has enough to go on.
Can reference earlier decisions and saved work.
userControls: Which workspace a conversation belongs to.
Whether you open a direct link or browse the sidebar.
How clearly you describe the conversation you want it to find.

thingsToKnow.summary: The sidebar list isn't the full record.
thingsToKnow.detail: A conversation can be missing from the sidebar but still open from a direct link or be recoverable by support.

thingsToKnow.summary: The newest messages take a moment to be findable.
thingsToKnow.detail: Search runs on stored history, so very recent messages can lag slightly before they turn up.

primitives.label: Integrations
primitives.tagline: Connected tools, data access, and API keys.
primitives.summary: The parent view for connected tools: native sign-ins (Slack, Google Drive, Notion), data access, longer-tail apps through Pipedream, and stored API keys. Slack, Google Drive, and Notion also keep their own cards.
productFeatures: Native sign-in for Slack, Google Drive, and Notion.
Data access through Motion's own commands.
Longer-tail apps through Pipedream, plus stored API keys where supported.
userControls: Which integrations you connect.
Which account, workspace, or data source is in play.
Which keys or longer-tail tools you've set up.

thingsToKnow.summary: Sign-in apps: one connection each for now. API keys: as many as you want.
thingsToKnow.detail: Slack, Google Drive, Notion, and Pipedream apps allow one connection per VM today, with more on the way. Anything set up with an API key can run several at once, each saved under its own name, for example two accounts or two environments.

tiers.label: Native OAuth
tiers.what: Built directly into Runneth with Motion-owned OAuth and clearer scope control.

tiers.label: Data access
tiers.what: Motion data, external endpoints, and CLI-backed data access. This includes Motion CLI, Meta data, TikTok data, Organic data, Motion reports, InSpo, workspace context, brand context, workspace goal, and spend threshold.

tiers.label: Pipedream / long-tail
tiers.what: Connected apps outside the native OAuth set. Use this for app-specific access that is not Slack, Google Drive, Notion, or Motion platform data.

tiers.label: Secrets / API keys
tiers.what: Stored API keys for tools without OAuth. Secrets should be collected through secure input, never pasted in chat.

primitives.label: Slack
primitives.summary: Getting Runneth into channels, posting replies and reports, how it behaves in threads, and reconnecting. Once it's in a channel, anyone there can tag it and get an answer in the thread.
productFeatures: Connects to Slack through a normal sign-in.
Reads channels and threads once it's been added to them.
Posts replies, reports, and briefs where it has access.
userControls: Which channels you invite it into.
Whether you want the reply in the channel or inside a thread.
When to reconnect Slack if it drops.

channelTypes.label: Public channel
rules: Anyone in the workspace can add Runneth, or it can add itself when asked.
It only reads the public channels it's been added to.

channelTypes.label: Private channel
rules: Someone already in the channel has to invite it. It can't add itself.
It only reads the private channels it's been invited to.

channelTypes.label: Direct message (Messages tab)
rules: Open Runneth from its Messages tab and it answers there. That thread is the supported way to work one-on-one.
It ignores plain one-line DMs sent outside a thread, and it can't start a DM with you first.

channelTypes.label: Group DM
rules: Not supported today. Slack blocks adding a bot to an existing group chat.

channelTypes.label: Slack Connect (external)
rules: Runneth stays out of externally shared channels, even if someone adds it.

thingsToKnow.summary: Tag once, then it stays in the thread.
thingsToKnow.detail: After it's pulled into a thread, anyone can keep replying without tagging it again.

thingsToKnow.summary: Whoever's in the channel can reach it.
thingsToKnow.detail: Once Runneth is in a channel, anyone there can tag it and it'll answer with your org's context. Add it only where that's fine.

primitives.label: Google Drive
primitives.tagline: Google Drive and Google file access.
primitives.summary: Connecting Drive and working with Google files: Docs, Sheets, Slides, picking files, and access issues. Use this for anything Drive-specific.
productFeatures: Connects to Google through a normal sign-in.
Reads the Google files you've given it access to.
Works with Docs, Sheets, Slides, and other supported Drive files.
userControls: Which files or folders you share with it.
Which Google account is connected.
Whether the exact file it needs has been granted.

thingsToKnow.summary: It only sees files you've shared with it.
thingsToKnow.detail: If a file won't open, it usually needs to be granted access, not a full reconnect. You can pick files to share at any time.

primitives.label: Notion
primitives.summary: Connecting Notion and reading the pages or databases you've shared. Use this for Notion access, permissions, and reading or querying issues.
productFeatures: Connects to Notion through a normal sign-in.
Reads and queries the pages or databases Notion gives it access to.
userControls: Which Notion workspace is connected.
Which pages or databases are shared with it.
When to reconnect or update permissions.

thingsToKnow.summary: Pages have to be shared before it can read them.
thingsToKnow.detail: A brand-new page won't be visible until you give the integration access to it.

primitives.label: Apps
primitives.tagline: Openable pages and dashboards Runneth builds.
primitives.summary: The pages Runneth creates that you can open: reports, dashboards, status pages, and previews. Use this for anything about a generated app, its link, or whether it's visible.
productFeatures: Builds openable pages for reports, dashboards, and previews.
Shows the data from the files Runneth saves behind the app.
Refreshes when Runneth reruns the data behind it.
userControls: What app you want built or refreshed.
Which files or data the app shows.
Whether it stays internal or gets shared more broadly.

thingsToKnow.summary: Apps are private to your workspace by default.
thingsToKnow.detail: Only people in the workspace that created the app can open it, unless you ask to share it more widely.

thingsToKnow.summary: Apps show saved data, refreshed on a schedule.
thingsToKnow.detail: A number you just changed can lag until the next refresh.

primitives.label: Routines
primitives.summary: Anything that runs later or on repeat: scheduling, reminders, monitoring, posting on a cadence, or keeping something updated. Use this for work that happens in the future rather than right now.
productFeatures: Future, recurring, scheduled, or background work.
Saving a routine plan now so it's ready to set up.
Steady refresh jobs when they're clearly spelled out.
userControls: What the routine should do.
The schedule, trigger, or condition.
Where it posts or what it refreshes, like a Slack thread, an app page, or a file.

thingsToKnow.summary: Reliable routine automation is still rolling out.
thingsToKnow.detail: Runneth can save the plan and set up a best-effort version now, but don't treat live scheduling as fully dependable yet. Keep a human backstop on anything time-sensitive.

thingsToKnow.summary: Slack-delivery routines are the newest piece.
thingsToKnow.detail: Posting on a schedule into Slack is coming soon and is the least proven part today.

primitives.label: Data access
primitives.tagline: Motion data and connected data sources.
primitives.summary: Where the numbers come from: your own Meta and TikTok performance, saved reports, brand context, goals, and competitor research through InSpo. Use this for anything about data pulls.
productFeatures: Pulls your own account's Meta and TikTok performance.
Reads your saved Motion reports, goals, and brand context.
Pulls competitor and external-brand research through InSpo.
userControls: Which workspace, account, platform, or date range to use.
Whether to rank by your saved goal, a specific metric, or a saved report.
Whether a spend cutoff applies, instead of filtering quietly.

boxes.label: Your performance
boxes.summary: Your own account's Meta and TikTok ad performance: spend, results, creative breakdowns, and trends.

boxes.label: Saved reports
boxes.summary: The Motion reports already saved in your workspace, used as the source of truth for those views.

boxes.label: Brand context
boxes.summary: Your own brand's voice, positioning, products, audience, and claims, used to ground strategy and copy.

boxes.label: Goal & metrics
boxes.summary: Your saved business goal and how results are measured, so best and worst line up with how you actually grade the account.

boxes.label: InSpo (competitors)
boxes.summary: Competitor and external-brand creatives and context for research. A separate source from your own-account data.

thingsToKnow.summary: Your Meta data comes through Motion, not a key you manage.
thingsToKnow.detail: Own-account Meta and TikTok numbers come through Motion's own connection. There's no separate Meta token for you to set up or worry about expiring.

thingsToKnow.summary: Your account and competitors are different sources.
thingsToKnow.detail: Your own performance comes from your connected accounts. Competitor and external-brand research comes from InSpo. They don't mix.

thingsToKnow.summary: More InSpo is on the way.
thingsToKnow.detail: Today InSpo covers competitor creatives and competitor brand context. Coming soon: InSpo brands, unique creatives, boards, creators, and TikTok organic posts.
